security-spec.md:64 (Trust Boundaries B3 row) and security-spec.md:74 (STRIDE Analysis B3 row) both describe the SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate's mitigation as purely existence-based: 'activation is machine-detected by plain file-existence of Epic A1's own canonical artifacts on main ... never by commit-ancestry alone' (line 64), and the STRIDE mitigation claims the design ensures 'never an unexplained or indefinitely-extended SKIP after its own dependency has actually landed' (line 74). This is now factually stale: design.md's revised SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate (design.md:1245-1274, this round's change) makes activation require BOTH (a) the owning task starting AND (b) artifact existence -- so a case CAN now remain a valid, non-failing SKIP indefinitely after Epic A1's artifacts land, for as long as the owning task (e.g. T-005 for AC-006) never starts. security-spec.md's STRIDE B3 mitigation text was not updated alongside this round's design.md revision and its claim ('never ... indefinitely-extended SKIP after its own dependency has actually landed') is no longer accurate; the corresponding residual risk (indefinite fail-open SKIP contingent on an owning task never starting, independent of Epic A1's merge state) is undocumented and unmitigated in security-spec.md. Per role instructions to treat layer specifications as normative refinements of design.md and report contradictions between them, this is a cross-layer inconsistency that must be corrected before this security posture can be relied on.

This round's design.md revision (SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate, design.md:1230-1293) correctly fixes the activation predicate to require BOTH (a) the owning task's substantive verification having started AND (b) canonical Epic A1 artifacts existing on main, and its own prose correctly resolves the T-001/AC-006 contradiction the revision exists to close (design.md:1250-1260: 'T-001 carries AC-006 presence-only, so AC-006's SKIP stays non-failing for the whole of T-001 regardless of Epic A1's merge state, and activates when T-005 starts'). However, that fix was not propagated to at least 9 other places in this same normative document set that restate the SAME mechanism using the OLD, pre-revision, single-clause trigger ('SKIP ... until Epic A1 merges', i.e. artifact-existence alone): design.md Architecture diagram CANARY node label (line 36: 'SKIP until Epic A1'); design.md Cross-Layer Dependencies (lines 205-209: 'until Epic A1 merges, AC-006/AC-015/AC-016 stay SKIP'); design.md API/Contract Plan item 1 (lines 969-974: 'a stale post-A1-merge SKIP does'); design.md Test Strategy item 1 (line 1059: canary case 'SKIPped ... until Epic A1 merges'); design.md Test Strategy item 5 (lines 1098-1100: 'SKIP ... is valid only until Epic A1 merges (AC-015)'); design.md Deployment/CI Plan (lines 1480-1492: 'Before Epic A1 merges ... an allowlisted SKIP ... is valid until then ... Once Epic A1 merges ... becomes both this epic's own Done gate and a required release gate'); acceptance-tests.md rows for AC-006, AC-015, AC-016, AC-028 (lines 10, 19, 20, 32: each says 'named SKIP until Epic A1 merges' or 'SKIP before Epic A1 merges'); and frontend-spec.md's Dependencies table (line 47: 'AC-006/AC-015/AC-016 stay SKIP ... until Epic A1 merges'). Since the review's own stated premise is that Epic A1 already merged on 2026-08-08, a reader who consults any of these 9 restatements instead of the one canonical Gate section would conclude AC-006/AC-015/AC-016 are already hard failures today -- recreating the exact T-001-unsatisfiable-contract defect this design revision exists to close. The revised predicate is correct in its one authoritative location but the contradiction has been moved, not eliminated, from the design read as a whole. Separately, per-case ownership is unambiguous for AC-006 (design.md:1257-1258 names 'T-005's exclusive scope' as a single task) but is NOT unambiguous for AC-015/AC-016: design.md:1260-1261 states only 'AC-015 and AC-016 activate with the tasks that seed their own allowlist entries (T-008 onward)' -- plural 'tasks' and an open-ended 'T-008 onward' range name no single task whose start satisfies activation clause (a) for either case, unlike AC-006's single named T-005. Additionally, design.md:1255-1258's own claim that AC-006's T-005 ownership is a fact 'the Automated/Manual Classification Table above assigns' is not actually supported by that table: the Automated/Manual Classification Table (design.md:1294-1328) has exactly four columns (Check (AC), Current Classification, Upgrade Condition, Gating fact/reason) and contains no task-ownership column or T-005 reference anywhere; the T-005 attribution exists only as freestanding prose inside the SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate section itself, so the cross-reference to the Classification Table as its source is inaccurate.
